legacy_delta: 2026-07-28 REMOVES the `initialize`/`initialized` handshake and `ping` method entirely; protocol is now fully stateless per-request. Every request carries `_meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion']` (required) and `_meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities']` (required); no session-level capability negotiation exists (schema.json $defs).
New method `server/discover` (server/discover.md) replaces `initialize` as an optional, idempotent, cacheable capability/version probe; servers MUST implement it, clients MAY call it.

New method `subscriptions/listen` (patterns/subscriptions.md) replaces the 2025-11-25 `resources/subscribe`/`resources/unsubscribe` RPCs and the deprecated HTTP GET/SSE stream endpoint; it is a single long-lived request whose reply is an open notification stream, filtered via a `notifications` object (`toolsListChanged`, `promptsListChanged`, `resourcesListChanged`, `resourceSubscriptions: string[]`).

New pattern 'Multi Round-Trip Requests' (MRTR, patterns/mrtr.md) REPLACES all server-initiated JSON-RPC requests (old `sampling/createMessage`, `elicitation/create`, `roots/list` sent server->client mid-request). Now servers return `resultType: "input_required"` (InputRequiredResult with `inputRequests`/`requestState`) on `tools/call`, `resources/read`, `prompts/get` ONLY, and the client re-issues the ORIGINAL request (new JSON-RPC id) with the answers as `inputResponses`. This is called out as an explicit breaking change ('The previous pattern of server-initiated requests is no longer supported').

Every JSON-RPC result now MUST carry a top-level `resultType` field ('complete' | 'input_required' | extension-defined); absent resultType from an older server MUST be treated as 'complete' for backward compat.
New `CacheableResult` base type adds `cacheScope` ('public'|'private') and `ttlMs` for client-side response caching (currently only used by DiscoverResult per schema/docs).

Three new error codes reserved/defined in the MCP sub-range -32020..-32099: -32020 HeaderMismatchError, -32021 MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError, -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersionError. Codes -32000..-32019 are frozen 'legacy', MUST NOT be newly allocated.

Old error code -32002 (resource not found, 2025-11-25 and earlier) is retired, replaced by generic -32602 Invalid params; new servers MUST NOT emit -32002, but clients SHOULD still accept it from legacy servers. -32042 (URL elicitation required, 2025-11-25 only) is likewise retired.

Extension negotiation is now generalized under `capabilities.extensions` (map of prefixed extension id -> settings object), e.g. `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` (MCP Apps) and `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` (Tasks) — both are OFFICIAL EXTENSIONS, not core; core schema.json has no Apps/Tasks-specific definitions.

New reserved _meta keys not present in 2025-11-25: `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`, `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`, `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`, `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel`, `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`, `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo`, plus OpenTelemetry `traceparent`/`tracestate`/`baggage` as an explicit unprefixed exception.

Streamable HTTP transport: new mandatory `MCP-Protocol-Version` header per POST (mismatch with body => 400 + HeaderMismatchError), and new REQUIRED envelope headers `Mcp-Method` (all requests) and `Mcp-Name` (tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get) mirroring body fields for intermediary routing; new optional `x-mcp-header`/`Mcp-Param-{name}` tool-parameter-to-header extension mechanism. GET stream endpoint removed vs. 2025-03-26 HTTP+SSE transport.

Dual-era compatibility matrix defined in versioning.md: legacy clients speaking `initialize` against a modern-only server fail with no fallback; dual-era servers must detect era per-request (presence of `_meta` protocol fields vs. an `initialize` call) and MAY serve both eras concurrently on the same endpoint/process.

methods.name: server/discover
methods.params: none beyond standard request fields + required _meta (protocolVersion, clientCapabilities; clientInfo optional)
methods.result: DiscoverResult(resultType, supportedVersions: string[], capabilities: ServerCapabilities, instructions?: string, _meta[serverInfo]?, cacheScope?, ttlMs?) — extends CacheableResult
methods.notes: MUST be implemented by servers (server/discover.md L11). Optional for clients to call. Used as stdio backward-compat probe.

methods.name: subscriptions/listen
methods.result: long-lived stream; first message is notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged (server->client) carrying io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId=request id; then filtered notifications; eventual SubscriptionsListenResult (resultType complete) on graceful close
methods.notes: replaces resources/subscribe + GET SSE endpoint. Server MUST NOT send unsubscribed notification types. Ack MUST precede all other stream notifications (per-subscription-ID ordering, not per-channel).

methods.name: resources/list
methods.notes: capability gate: server must declare resources capability

methods.name: tools/call
methods.result: CallToolResult(content: ContentBlock[], isError?, structuredContent?) OR InputRequiredResult

methods.name: roots/list
methods.direction: server->client (as an MRTR inputRequest, never a bare server-initiated JSON-RPC request)
methods.notes: client roots capability; only ever appears as a value inside InputRequests map (mrtr.md)

methods.name: sampling/createMessage
methods.notes: client sampling capability; MRTR-only, never top-level server-initiated request

methods.name: elicitation/create
methods.params: ElicitRequestParams — union of ElicitRequestFormParams{mode:'form', message, requestedSchema} and ElicitRequestURLParams (per schema $defs)

methods.name: notifications/cancelled
methods.direction: notification client->server (normal use) or server->client (subscriptions/listen teardown only)
methods.notes: Server MUST send this ONLY to terminate a subscriptions/listen stream; MUST NOT use it for any other purpose (mrtr note in ClientNotification description, cancellation.md #2).

methods.name: notifications/progress
methods.notes: progress MUST strictly increase; requires opting in via _meta.progressToken on the original request

methods.name: notifications/resources/list_changed
methods.notes: only sent inside an active subscriptions/listen stream with resourcesListChanged filter set

methods.name: notifications/resources/updated
methods.notes: only for URIs listed in resourceSubscriptions filter of an active subscription

methods.name: notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged
methods.notes: MUST be first message on a subscriptions/listen stream, before any other notification on that subscription

requirements.text: All messages MUST follow JSON-RPC 2.0; requests MUST include a non-null string/integer id, unique among in-flight requests from the sender.
Result responses MUST include a resultType field; unrecognized resultType values MUST be treated as invalid by the client; absent resultType (older server) MUST be treated as 'complete'.
Servers MUST NOT initiate JSON-RPC requests; clients do not send JSON-RPC responses. All server->client requests happen only via MRTR's InputRequiredResult mechanism.

Every request MUST carry io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities in _meta; a request missing a required field is malformed and MUST be rejected by the server with -32602 Invalid params (400 Bad Request on HTTP).
Clients SHOULD include io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo on every request unless configured not to.

If a request requires a capability the client did not declare in clientCapabilities, server MUST return MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021) with data.requiredCapabilities; HTTP status MUST be 400.
Servers SHOULD include io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo in every result's _meta unless configured not to.
clientInfo/serverInfo are self-reported and unverified; implementations SHOULD NOT use them to change behavior or rely on them for security decisions.
On a subscriptions/listen stream, server MUST include io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId in every delivered notification's _meta.

Implementations MUST NOT automatically dereference $ref values pointing to a network URI in JSON Schemas; an opt-in fetch mode MUST be disabled by default and enforce host allowlist/reject loopback/private addresses/timeouts/size limits/logging.
Clients and servers MUST support JSON Schema 2020-12 for schemas without explicit $schema; MUST validate per declared/default dialect and handle unsupported dialects with an appropriate error.
Clients that render icons MUST support image/png and image/jpeg (and image/jpg); SHOULD also support image/svg+xml and image/webp.

Icon consumers MUST reject icon URIs using unsafe schemes/redirects (javascript:, file:, ftp:, ws:, local app schemes), disallow cross-origin scheme changes/redirects, fetch icons without credentials, verify same-origin as the server, and validate MIME type via magic bytes (reject on mismatch).
Servers MUST implement server/discover.
On unsupported/unknown requested protocol version, server MUST respond with UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022) listing data.supported and data.requested.
Client SHOULD select a mutually supported version from the error's 'supported' list and retry, or surface an error to the user if none exists.

Extension identifiers in capabilities.extensions MUST follow _meta key naming rules with a mandatory prefix; if one party lacks support for an advertised extension it MUST revert to core behavior or reject with an appropriate error.
A server implementing only modern versions SHOULD (recommendation, not MUST) name its supported protocol versions in any error returned to a legacy initialize request, on any transport.
Server MUST NOT send notification types on a subscriptions/listen stream that the client did not request in its notifications filter.

Server MUST send notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged as the first message of a subscription, carrying the subscriptionId, before any other notification on that subscription (ordering scoped per-subscription-id, interleaving from other subscriptions allowed on stdio).
On stdio, clients MUST use io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId to demultiplex notifications since all messages share one channel.
When the server ends a subscription on its own initiative it SHOULD send a graceful-close SubscriptionsListenResult (resultType complete) before closing the stream.
On stdio, after a reconnection the client MUST re-send subscriptions/listen; the server holds no subscription state across reconnects.

Servers MUST send server-to-client requests (roots/list, sampling/createMessage, elicitation/create) using the MRTR pattern; the previous server-initiated-request pattern is no longer supported (breaking change).
Servers MAY respond to prompts/get, resources/read, tools/call only with InputRequiredResult; MUST NOT do so for any other client request.
inputRequests keys MUST be unique within the request scope; values MUST be one of ElicitRequest, CreateMessageRequest, ListRootsRequest.

If requestState influences authorization/resource access/business logic, servers MUST protect its integrity (HMAC/AEAD) and MUST reject state failing verification; integrity protection MAY be omitted only if tampering causes nothing worse than request failure.
Servers for which requestState must be single-use MUST enforce that invariant server-side (replay-window controls alone are insufficient).
Servers MUST include at least one of inputRequests or requestState in every InputRequiredResult.
Servers MUST NOT send an inputRequests entry whose method the client hasn't declared capability support for (e.g. elicitation/create requires client elicitation capability).
Servers MUST NOT assume clients will fulfill inputRequests or retry.
If InputRequiredResult has inputRequests, client MUST construct the requested inputs before retrying; if absent, client MAY retry immediately.
Client MUST echo requestState verbatim on retry if present, and MUST NOT include one if absent; MUST NOT inspect/parse/modify requestState.
The JSON-RPC id MUST differ between the initial request and the retry (independent requests).
inputRequests/requestState fields from one InputRequiredResult MUST NOT be applied to any other parallel request.

On malformed/invalid InputResponses, server SHOULD return a JSON-RPC error with appropriate code/message; unexpected extra params SHOULD be ignored; missing required info SHOULD produce a new InputRequiredResult rather than an error.
Cancellation notifications from the server (notifications/cancelled) MUST reference a subscriptions/listen request id only; MUST NOT be used for any other purpose.
Streamable HTTP: a client disconnect (closing the SSE response stream) MUST be treated by the server as cancellation of that request; no notifications/cancelled is required.
On stdio there is no per-request stream to close; client MUST send notifications/cancelled referencing the request id to cancel.
Implementations SHOULD establish timeouts for all sent requests and SHOULD always enforce a maximum timeout regardless of progress notifications.
Progress tokens MUST be a string or integer, unique across active requests.
Progress value MUST strictly increase with each notification even if total is unknown; notifications MUST stop after completion.
JSON-RPC messages MUST be UTF-8 encoded on every transport.
Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming Streamable HTTP connections; if Origin is present and invalid, server MUST reject appropriately.
Client MUST use HTTP POST for every JSON-RPC message; MUST include an Accept header listing both application/json and text/event-stream; MUST include request-metadata headers on each POST.

Server MUST return 202 Accepted for an accepted notification/response POST, or an HTTP error status if it cannot accept the message; a response POST returns Content-Type application/json or text/event-stream.
Server SHOULD include X-Accel-Buffering: no on SSE responses to defeat proxy buffering; SHOULD periodically emit SSE comment lines as heartbeats.
Resumable SSE via Last-Event-ID is NOT supported in this revision.
Every POST to the MCP endpoint MUST include an MCP-Protocol-Version header; mismatched value vs. the body's _meta protocol version MUST yield 400 Bad Request + HeaderMismatch JSON-RPC error.
A server implementing 2025-06-18 semantics (which predates the MCP-Protocol-Version header) MAY treat a request omitting the header as protocol version 2025-03-26.
Mcp-Method header (mirroring params.method) is REQUIRED on all requests; Mcp-Name (mirroring params.name or params.uri) is REQUIRED for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get.
If the Mcp-Name source value cannot be safely represented as a plain ASCII header value, client MUST Base64-encode it using the sentinel format defined in the spec.
Clients supporting x-mcp-header annotations MUST mirror the designated tool parameter values into HTTP headers named Mcp-Param-{name}.
x-mcp-header values MUST be case-insensitively unique among all such values in a tool's schema and MUST only appear directly under a properties key (else invalid).
On stdio, a dual-era client SHOULD send server/discover first as backward-compat probe; falls back to initialize on any non-modern error/timeout.
Servers MUST NOT emit error codes -32002 or -32042 (retired 2025-11-25-and-earlier codes); clients SHOULD still accept -32002 from legacy servers.

New codes in -32020..-32099 MUST be defined exclusively by the MCP spec; implementations MUST NOT emit undefined codes from this sub-range, and MUST NOT allocate new codes in the frozen -32000..-32019 legacy sub-range.
New error codes for non-spec purposes SHOULD be allocated outside the JSON-RPC reserved range (-32768..-32000).
Notifications MUST NOT include an id field.

Servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests over the same connection to establish context (statelessness); state spanning requests MUST be referenced by an explicit identifier the client passes each request.

Content-Type values: application/json (single JSON-RPC object response) or text/event-stream (SSE). HTTP status codes: 202 Accepted (notification/response POST accepted), 400 Bad Request (header mismatch, missing required _meta fields, malformed legacy initialize against modern-only server).

Extension identifiers observed as examples (not core schema defs): io.modelcontextprotocol/ui (MCP Apps extension, settings e.g. {mimeTypes:['text/html;profile=mcp-app']}), io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks (Tasks extension, empty settings object = support with defaults). These live in capabilities.extensions map, not in $defs.
Icon MIME types: clients MUST support image/png, image/jpeg/image/jpg; SHOULD support image/svg+xml, image/webp. Icon.src MUST be https: or data: URI only.
JSON Schema dialect default: JSON Schema 2020-12 (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema) when $schema absent; implementations MUST support at least 2020-12.
sdk_implications: A PowerShell SDK cannot model MCP as a stateful 'session' object with Initialize()/Connect() semantics the way older SDKs did; every outgoing request builder (client and server dispatch) MUST inject the three _meta fields (protocolVersion required, clientCapabilities required, clientInfo recommended) on EVERY call, not once at connection setup. This is a fundamental architecture decision to make explicit in the plan.

No 'ping' keepalive RPC exists; if the PowerShell SDK wants a liveness check it must use server/discover (cacheable) or transport-level mechanisms, not invent a 'Ping-McpServer' cmdlet that maps to a wire method.

Server-side SDK must NOT expose sampling/createMessage, elicitation/create, roots/list as things a tool handler can 'send and await' synchronously mid-call in the old server-initiated-request style; instead the SDK's tool-handler API must support returning an InputRequiredResult (pluggable 'need more input' outcome) and resuming from a subsequent request carrying inputResponses + requestState — this needs a distinct PowerShell cmdlet/object model (e.g. New-McpInputRequired, a Resume-McpToolCall path) rather than blocking calls.

Client-side SDK must implement InputRequiredResult handling as a retry loop: same original params + a freshly generated request id + inputResponses + verbatim requestState, and must never let user code inspect/mutate requestState.

Client SDK needs first-class support for subscriptions/listen as a distinct long-lived streaming call type (not a fire-and-forget notification handler), with subscription-id-based demultiplexing baked into the transport abstraction for stdio, and native reliance on the HTTP response stream's lifetime for Streamable HTTP.

Error handling layer must special-case resultType alongside JSON-RPC error responses: success path is no longer just 'no error field' — must branch on resultType complete vs input_required vs unknown (throw) vs missing (treat as complete for legacy interop).

SDK must implement the -32020/-32021/-32022 error types as strongly-typed PowerShell exceptions/error records with their `data` payloads (data.requiredCapabilities for -32021, data.supported/data.requested for -32022), and must never emit -32002/-32042 while still being able to parse them from legacy peers if dual-era support is planned.

HTTP transport implementation must set Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name/MCP-Protocol-Version headers on every POST derived from the JSON-RPC body, implement Base64 sentinel encoding for unsafe Mcp-Name values, and support the optional x-mcp-header/Mcp-Param-{name} mirroring for tool parameters flagged in tool JSON schemas.

Because the protocol is stateless, the PowerShell server SDK should not assume one process/runspace = one client; concurrent/interleaved requests from unrelated logical conversations over the same stdio pipe must be supported, which affects how request dispatch and cancellation tracking are scoped (per request id, not per connection).

Cancellation must be transport-differentiated: stdio path sends notifications/cancelled; Streamable HTTP path relies on stream/connection closing — SDK's cancellation token plumbing must map to the right primitive per transport and the server must treat HTTP disconnect as an implicit cancel signal.

If dual-era (2025-11-25/legacy) interop is in scope, the SDK needs a distinct legacy code path implementing the old initialize handshake, ping, resources/subscribe, and server-initiated requests, selected via the era-detection probe (server/discover on stdio; a 4xx/error-shape check on HTTP) — this roughly doubles the surface area versus targeting 2026-07-28 alone, and should be an explicit go/no-go decision in the plan.
open_questions: Is dual-era (2025-11-25 and earlier) interoperability in scope for v1 of the PowerShell SDK, or is 2026-07-28-only acceptable? This materially changes the design (need for legacy initialize/ping/subscribe code paths).

Are the io.modelcontextprotocol/ui (MCP Apps) and io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks (Tasks) extensions in scope? They are official but not part of core schema.json/$defs — no type definitions for them were found in the read schema; would need separate extension spec pages fetched if required.

The exact JSON shape/required fields of ElicitRequestFormParams vs ElicitRequestURLParams, PrimitiveSchemaDefinition variants (Boolean/Number/String/Enum/MultiSelectEnum/SingleSelectEnum + Titled/Untitled/Legacy variants), and ToolAnnotations/ToolChoice were not read field-by-field in this pass (only enumerated by name) — needs a follow-up read of schema.json bodies for those defs before finalizing the PowerShell type model.

The custom-header x-mcp-header schema extension section (streamable-http.md ~L357-410) was only partially read; exact validation rules (case-insensitive uniqueness scope, nesting restriction wording) should be re-verified in full before encoding as SDK validation logic.

Whether InputRequest/InputResponse (singular) $defs differ meaningfully from InputRequests/InputResponses (the maps) was not verified — likely singular defs are the union element type, but not confirmed from schema.json body text.

Server capabilities' exact shape (ServerCapabilities/ClientCapabilities $defs) including which capability keys exist (tools, resources, prompts, sampling, roots, elicitation, completions, logging, extensions, etc.) was inferred from usage examples, not from directly reading those two $defs' property lists — needs confirmation before finalizing capability-gating code.

summary: 2026-07-28 is a ground-up rewrite of MCP's core protocol relative to 2025-11-25: it drops the stateful `initialize`/`ping` handshake and all server-initiated JSON-RPC requests in favor of (1) fully stateless per-request `_meta` fields (protocolVersion, clientCapabilities required; clientInfo, logLevel optional) on every message, (2) an optional `server/discover` method for capability/version probing, replacing initialize, (3) a new "Multi Round-Trip Requests" (MRTR) pattern where servers signal need for client input via `resultType: "input_required"` (InputRequiredResult) on only `tools/call`/`resources/read`/`prompts/get`, and the client retries the SAME logical request (new id) with `inputResponses` + echoed opaque `requestState` — sampling/createMessage, elicitation/create, and roots/list now only ever appear inside this InputRequests map, never as bare server->client requests, and (4) `subscriptions/listen`, a single long-lived request replacing `resources/subscribe`/GET-SSE, filtered by a notifications object and demultiplexed via `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`. Every result now carries `resultType` ('complete'|'input_required', extensible); CacheableResult adds `cacheScope`/`ttlMs` for `server/discover`. Three new error codes occupy the -32020..-32099 MCP-reserved sub-range: HeaderMismatchError (-32020), MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021), UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022); old -32002/-32042 are retired. Streamable HTTP transport requires `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name` headers mirroring body fields, drops the GET stream endpoint and Last-Event-ID resumption, and adds an `x-mcp-header`/`Mcp-Param-{name}` tool-parameter-to-header extension. Extensions (e.g. MCP Apps `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`, Tasks `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`) are negotiated via `capabilities.extensions`, outside core schema.json. schema.json enumerates 155 $defs (full list below); `InitializeRequest`, `PingRequest`, `SetLevelRequest`, resource subscribe/unsubscribe requests, and `notifications/roots/list_changed` are all absent versus earlier revisions, confirming their removal. Dual-era (legacy+modern) coexistence is explicitly specified with a compatibility matrix and stdio/HTTP-specific era-detection probes, which a PowerShell SDK targeting only 2026-07-28 could skip but a dual-era SDK could not.
